title: Choose the visual world for Six Hats
question: The roll assigned The Count. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Count
options.lineage: the secret ballot and the counting hall
options.thesis: Every hat is a ballot: marks are made in private, sealed, and counted open together at 0:00.
options.viewport: Top bar with session and code; the open hat as a ballot header with its prompt and a big tabular countdown; your sealed slips beside the register of who has marked.
options.risk: Could read as political or drift into cream paper; held to paper, ink and the count, with no symbols, flags or ballot-box clichés.

raised.raise: States are printed marks at one rule weight: hairline at rest, filled when chosen, struck when disabled, bracketed on focus.
One type family on a strict size scale; every numeral tabular, so clocks and counts never jitter.
A visible 8px cell grid: every block snaps to it and reflows by whole cells.
Density courage: revealed slips pack edge to edge in whole cells, so a full room still fits one screen.
Neutrals come from one strict tonal ramp; no ad-hoc greys.

options.label: Night Line
options.lineage: a metropolitan rail diagram fired in midnight enamel
options.thesis: The session is a line: each hat a station, the current one burning brightest, the decision the terminus.
options.viewport: The flow drawn as a rail line across the top with the current station lit; the open hat's prompt, clock and points below; the register as a platform board.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity (anyone can follow the route from across a room), but loses the blind-and-count ritual that makes this product different. It also topped my own list, as a daylight map.
options.risk: A dark ground can wash out on lit-room projectors, and transit-map dashboards are a familiar move.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.lineage: a reference page ruled by engine
options.thesis: Two columns twinned round a rail of keys, the apparatus in a wide margin.
options.viewport: Points in two columns around a rail of hat keys.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a small, quiet scholarly page fails a screen-shared board.
options.kept: States as printed marks at one rule weight.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Pixel display type at poster scale over fine grotesk text.
options.viewport: A pixel-built hat name and clock towering over the points.
options.case: Fuses poorly: engineers like the pixels, but bitmap display fights calm and distance reading.
options.kept: One type family on a strict size scale; tabular numerals.

options.label: Crouwel Grid
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: A grid-built clock and hat name over a visible grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the lettering becomes the subject instead of the discussion.
options.kept: A visible cell grid every block snaps to.
options.risk: Design-poster costume on a working screen.

options.label: Circle Catalog
options.lineage: a convention circle catalog on newsprint
options.thesis: Stamp-sized cells packed in a numbered grid, circled in biro.
options.viewport: Every point a numbered cell; votes circled in pen.
options.case: Fuses poorly: fan-convention newsprint density reads as noise to a product team.
options.kept: Density courage: slips pack edge to edge in whole cells.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over an eleven-step zone ramp, hatched by load.
options.viewport: Each step a sheet slid over the last.
options.case: Fuses poorly: darkroom notation is foreign to the team and buries the hat in hatching.
options.kept: Neutrals from one strict tonal ramp.
options.risk: Opaque to anyone who never printed photos.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean retro-board app, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A left rail of steps, the current hat's cards in a column, a timer pill top right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every retro tool by design.
